page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-24-lssd belongs to the general-purpose C4 machine family, providing 24 virtual CPUs across 12 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. The instance utilizes the x86_64 architecture with hyperthreading, allocating two threads per physical core alongside a 504 MB L3 cache. It comes equipped with 90.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 3.75 GB per virtual core. Storage is provisioned via 1,608 GB of direct-attached NVMe local SSDs divided across four drives. Hardware-accelerated graphics are not present, as the server includes zero GPUs.

In benchmark testing, the instance exhibits top-tier single-threaded CPU capability, scoring 2,309.0 in Geekbench single-core evaluations and achieving 36.95 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. Text processing and small model LLM text generation also land in the top ten percent. Multi-core execution demonstrates strong throughput, reaching 16,269.0 points in Geekbench multi-core and delivering 46.34 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks. Conversely, heavier computational tasks show limitations: while medium model LLM text generation achieves 20.94 tokens/sec, large 70B model text generation falls to 2.39 tokens/sec, ranking in the bottom ten percent. Standard database operations and Redis SET workloads remain in the middle tier of benchmark results.

The integration of 1,608 GB local NVMe storage makes this instance balanced for operations requiring rapid scratch disk or database I/O, such as relational databases, caching layers, and high-throughput static web serving. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of bundled NVMe storage delivers high storage bandwidth without requiring separate persistent disk attachments, although data volatility on local SSDs requires appropriate application-level replication strategies. The machine is best suited for web serving, data processing pipelines, build environments, and transactional database workloads that fit within 90 GB of RAM.
